indexing.note: not indexed: the personal exemption steps up by a fixed 275 / 425 / 550 only on a revenue trigger and is already at its statutory cap (4,400 / 6,800 / 8,800); age-65 700 fixed (M.G.L. c. 62 s. 3(B)(b)(1))
fixed: 20,000, the New York cap (N.Y. Tax Law 612(c)(3-a)) that Massachusetts applies through TIR 95-9

not_modelled.what: A contributory public pension from a state other than New York: deductible up to what that state would exclude for a Massachusetts public pension, or in full if that state has no income tax (TIR 95-9). The amount depends on the other state's law and the sources name no state but New York, so it is not computed: the pension is taxed in full.
Exemptions for dependents (1,000 each) and blindness (2,200).
Deduction of up to 2,000 a person for Social Security and Medicare paid from wages.
Deductions for rent paid on a Massachusetts home and for student loan interest.
Exclusion for a firefighter or police officer incapacitated in the line of duty.
Collectibles gains: 12% rate with a 50% deduction.

approximations.what: Roth conversions are not in covers: the booklet does not say whether they qualify (covers_unclear in the record). If they do, this overstates tax in a conversion year.
approximations.size: Up to the state rate times the conversion, for a household inside a capped relief's room.

approximations.what: Massachusetts builds its own income definition; the projection starts from federal AGI.
approximations.size: Small for most retirees; differences include federal deductions Massachusetts doesn't allow.

approximations.what: IRA and employer-plan withdrawals are taxed in full; Massachusetts taxes them only above contributions already taxed by Massachusetts (the booklet's basis rule).
approximations.size: 5% of the Massachusetts basis recovered each year; larger for someone who contributed while living in Massachusetts.

approximations.what: The wage deduction for Social Security and Medicare paid is not applied.
approximations.size: Up to 5% of 2,000 = 100 a year per working person.

approximations.what: New York State contributory pension: the 59 1/2 age test is applied by age in the tax year; the sources don't say on what date it is measured (New York's own rule decides).
approximations.size: Only the year a person turns 59 1/2: up to 5% of 20,000 = 1,000.

approximations.what: Part-year residents moving from New York: the deduction is reduced by any amount New York excluded in the same year; the projection assumes a full-year resident.

derived_figures.what: 5% rate plus the 4% surtax over 1,083,150, folded into the brackets
short-term gains: 8.5% own rate less the 5% bracket rate
